correctness.rationale: The pair-state de Bruijn predecessor relations M0=323 and M1=49792 generate 120 Boolean relations, of which 75 have a diagonal. For cyclic outputs, diagonal relation products characterize same-period input existence even at n=1,2. The exact 120-coordinate identity P(T)f=-9e0 with Te0=0 gives the order-ten recurrence for all positive n; the first ten terms identify -zD'/D with D=(1+z^3-z^5)(1-2z+z^3-z^5). The polynomial root bounds, Rouché for the quartic quotient and triangle inequality for the other quintic, yield unique dominant lambda≈1.784598933 and O(1.5^n) error. A fresh independent relation representation confirmed 120/75, the full 120-coordinate identity, and exhaustive map images n<=10. Finite checking supports but does not replace the algebraic recurrence proof.
